card.cheat: Falling back to a different engine or row-limited chunks that change semantics; closed by exact-result gate over varied dtypes and null patterns, with memory measured in a fresh process.

card.title: Polars join peak-memory regression recovery

source_notes: repo https://github.com/pola-rs/polars; merged PR or fixed issue

facts.claim: pola-rs/polars issue #14201 exists: 'Intermittent out-of-memory performing join after 0.20.6 update', opened Feb 1, 2024, closed Feb 4, 2024

The regression was reported in Polars 0.20.6 (reporter says 0.20.5 was unaffected); symptom is memory growth until swap is exhausted on a left string-key join; casting the key to Categorical avoided it
The fix is PR #14264, titled 'fix: deduplicate recursive growables', merged Feb 4, 2024 as commit fd781eb, which 'Fixes #14201'
The public fix concerns recursive growables (nested-type gather), not hash build, partitioning or string gather as the seed's reference description states
PR #14264 diff size (files changed, lines added and deleted) and any benchmark or memory numbers
A python-polars release py-0.20.7 exists (Feb 4) and its notes contain no join-memory or regression fix; the only join bug fix is 'Fix join validation for String types' (#14229)
Repo is MIT-licensed, Rust, 40134 stars, release py-2.0.0 exists (from the GitHub API facts supplied in the seed)
The seed's measured reference speedup and memory on the generator, and the generated workload suite
Later join-path work on the same data exists upstream (seed's 'later join-path work' claim)

full_card.band: Optimization with 2^u-1 reward. Frontier likely reaches partial credit by locating the nested-growable memory cost. Whether a 8h frontier run reaches the reference depends on whether the reference needs multiple join paths beyond the PR; unverified. Score 3 without dated evidence.
full_card.build_cost: About 2-4 days: offline cargo vendor for polars, maturin build recipe, generator, exact-equality gate, RSS harness. Smoke build is empty so build time is unmeasured.
full_card.deliverable: Code changes in the Rust join path (and any gather/growable code it uses) that cut peak RSS and wall time for inner/left/semi joins on wide, skewed, string, categorical, null-key and multi-key frames, with results unchanged.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Exact-result gate over varied dtypes and null patterns; fresh-process RSS; no engine fallback (pandas or other) permitted; reject edits to grader, build config or vendored deps; history-less snapshot so PR #14264 cannot be read.
full_card.grading_surface: Generated join workloads (key skew, null keys, multi-key, many-to-many, sorted vs unsorted, string and categorical keys, nested columns). Exact-equality gate up to row order and dtypes; then median wall time and peak RSS in separate fresh-process runs, scored against reference.
full_card.local_fit: Rust release build plus Python wheel on 8 cores/16 GB under gVisor. Wall-clock and RSS timing are feasible but noisy; LTO builds may exceed 16 GB and be slow, so the agent needs a dev-like profile for iteration.
full_card.lookup: partial: the fix is public in git history (PR #14264, fd781eb) and is short; snapshot is history-less; a strong agent may recall the growable area in outline only.
full_card.provenance: Polars issue #14201 (OOM in left string-key join after 0.20.6, reporter david-waterworth) fixed by merged PR #14264 'fix: deduplicate recursive growables' (commit fd781eb, Feb 4 2024). MIT.
full_card.reference: Not built yet. Public upstream fix PR #14264 is a small recursive-growables dedupe, so the seed's multi-path reference is unverified; CG would need its own reference that meets the claimed speedup.
full_card.ships: History-less snapshot of the polars Rust core and Python bindings at the 0.20.6-era code, plus a pinned offline cargo vendor and a build recipe. Generator and grader withheld.

spike_plan.kill_if: The regression does not reproduce on 0.20.5 vs 0.20.6, or the PR alone closes the gap (one-lever, K10), or the release build cannot finish in the spike window.
spike_plan.pass_if: 0.20.6 is measurably worse than 0.20.5 in peak RSS or wall time on at least one join shape; the PR alone leaves a residual gap across several join paths; medians repeat within about 10%.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, pip install polars==0.20.5 and polars==0.20.6 into separate venvs (versions per the issue; confirm they exist on PyPI).

Write a generator: left table ~90k rows, 15 columns including nested list/struct columns and a String key; right lookup ~500 rows; also inner/left/semi variants, skewed keys, null keys, multi-key, categorical keys.

Run each join in a fresh process, recording median wall time (5 runs) and peak RSS via resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss. Confirm 0.20.6 is worse than 0.20.5 on at least one shape; if not, the regression is not reproduced and the idea is killed.

Check out the commit before fd781eb (PR #14264 parent) and build the Python wheel with maturin in release mode (budget up to 60 min; if the build exceeds this, stop and report build time). Compare the nested-growable fix alone against the 0.20.6 wheel on the same generator.

Decide scope: if the PR alone recovers most of the memory and time gap, the task is one-lever (K10/K8 risk) and must be reshaped; if a large gap remains on string or categorical joins, that gap defines the multi-path scope.
Check determinism: repeat medians on two runs; reject if the variance exceeds the expected gain.

v1.summary: The seed's regression is real: polars issue #14201 reports an OOM in a string-key left join from 0.20.6, closed by merged PR #14264 (fd781eb). That PR is a small "deduplicate recursive growables" fix, which contradicts the seed's multi-path reference (hash build, partitioning, string gather), so the 8h scope and reward cap need a spike before the task is built.
